correctness.rationale: Set A,B,C as selected column subsets in the outer/middle/outer K_n layers and a,b,c sizes. Direct neighborhood counts yield outer conditions a,c≥2 and required B coverage if an outer count equals two, plus separate middle conditions b=0,1,2,≥3. The proof divides minimal solutions into b=0,1,2,3,4 and excludes b≥5 because a middle vertex becomes redundant; in each case outer minimality and deletion of B vertices force a finite size profile. The resulting counts are the six terms using q=C(n−2,2), r=2q+C(n−2,3), h=C(n−3,3), j=C(n−3,2); n=6,7 coincident exponents are summed. Independently exhaustively checked all 2^18=262144 layer selections at n=6 by checking 3n neighbor inequalities and every one-vertex deletion; obtained 116290 feasible sets and minimal cardinality counts {6:15,7:600,8:1290,9:920,12:1}, matching the polynomial. The all-n proof rests on complete b-case arguments, not extrapolation from n=6.
